initial.reason: The evidence from https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli and related sources shows that mermaid-cli is a command-line tool that does not require authentication or credentials for use. This matches the claim of auth_methods: ["none"].
The rubric specifies that for open-source CLI tools with no hosted credentials, self_serve should be not_applicable. The evidence confirms mermaid-cli is a CLI tool with no credential concept.
The evidence and documentation confirm that mermaid-cli is a command-line interface only, not a REST or GraphQL API. This supports api_type: ["cli_only"].
There is no evidence of any app review process required for production use of mermaid-cli, as it is an open-source CLI tool. This supports app_review_required: false.

The verdict of not_applicable is correct per the rubric: open-source CLI/library with no hosted credentials concept should be marked not_applicable, with self_serve=not_applicable and auth_methods=[none]. The evidence and rubric are in agreement.

Multiple sources (https://transcriptapi.com/docs/mcp, https://transcriptapi.com) explicitly state that both OAuth2 and API key authentication are supported. For example: 'Authentication: OAuth 2.1 (Claude, ChatGPT) or an API key sent as a Bearer token (OpenAI Agent Builder and other clients).' and 'TranscriptAPI works with any platform that supports MCP. Whether your platform uses OAuth for seamless authentication (like Claude and ChatGPT) or requires manual API key configuration (like OpenAI Agent Builder), we provide both options.'

The main site and blog (https://transcriptapi.com, https://transcriptapi.com/blog/extract-youtube-transcripts-n8n-workflows) both state that users can sign up and get an API key with 100 free credits and no credit card required. Example: 'Sign up at transcriptapi.com and grab your key. You get 100 free credits. No credit card needed.'

The documentation (https://transcriptapi.com/docs/getting-started, https://transcriptapi.com) clearly states that TranscriptAPI offers a REST API and also supports integration via Model Context Protocol (MCP), which is used by SDKs/AI assistants. Example: 'Get YouTube video transcripts through our REST API or seamlessly integrate with AI assistants using Model Context Protocol (MCP).' and 'TranscriptAPI is a REST API, so any language that can send an HTTPS request with a Bearer API key can call it.'

There is no evidence in the documentation or main site that production use of the core API requires any app review. Users can sign up, get an API key, and use it immediately. OAuth client setup for MCP integrations is described, but there is no mention of a required app review for production use of the REST API or MCP server.

The evidence supports the rubric's requirements for 'buildable_now': the API is public, free self-serve credentials are available, and there is no indication of required app review or gating. The quoted text and documentation confirm all necessary criteria.

The documentation explicitly lists OAuth2 and Personal Access Token (API key) as supported authentication methods. OAuth2 is described for integrations, and Personal Access Token (PAT) is available for personal use. Workspace Access Token is also a form of API key.
Personal API access (via PAT) is available on every plan, including Free, and can be generated by users without contacting support or sales. This meets the rubric for free self-serve credentials.
The API is described as a REST API, with endpoints accessible via HTTP requests and standard RESTful patterns.

There is no evidence in the documentation that production use of the core API requires an app review. OAuth2 client registration is described as self-serve, and there is no mention of a review process for production use.
The evidence supports 'buildable_now': there is a documented public REST API, free self-serve credentials (PAT), and no indication of required app review or gating for production use.
